summary.text: A 199 m WWII troopship lying on its side off Luganville, reached from the beach. The bow sits near 20 m and the stern near 70 m, so most of it is deep and involves deco. Holds, jeeps and 'The Lady' statue make it a multi-day wreck.

s1.quote: Snorkel-friendly shallows down to depths exceeding 130 ft (40 m).

s2.quote: This is an extremely easy dive, either from the shore (so long as the seas are flat) or from a boat. … start following the wreckage to the west along the sand bottom (about 35 meters)

highlights.text: Bulldozers, trucks and jeeps dumped after WWII

summary.text: A slope off Luganville where the US military pushed surplus vehicles and machinery into the sea after WWII. Easy from the beach in calm weather; wreckage runs from the shallows to about 35-40 m.

s1.quote: Long fingers covered in yellow, blue and green staghorn coral drop down to a depth of more than 30 metres. … This huge field of staghorn coral comes to within six metres of the surface.

summary.text: A big staghorn coral field near Hideaway Island off Efate, with the reef beginning about 6 m below the surface and falling away past 30 m. Damselfish and anemones live among the branches.

s1.quote: The Cathedral is a striking tall narrow cavern, about a 20-minute boat ride from Port Vila. … The entrance to the cavern is tall and wide, about 22m deep at the sandy bottom

s2.quote: an impressive tall narrow cavern stretching down to 28m

highlights.text: Chimney to the surface beyond the pulpit

summary.text: A tall, narrow cavern a short boat ride from Port Vila, with a wide entrance on a sandy floor around 22-28 m and a chimney that lets divers surface inside.
